headline: Mitchell Starc's 6-wicket haul: Bangladesh bowled out for 64 in Test
summary: Australia's Mitchell Starc devastated the batting lineup, taking 6 wickets for just 12 runs in a crushing blow to the Tigers.
details: Bangladesh was bowled out for just 64 runs in their first innings of a Test match against Australia in Mackay, with Mitchell Starc leading the charge.
Starc's devastating spell of 10 overs took the Tigers' batting lineup apart, leaving them all out in just 34 overs. This marks Bangladesh's fourth-lowest team total in Test history.
The collapse happened rapidly. Within the first 7 overs of the morning session, Bangladesh lost 5 wickets for 12 runs, with four of the top six batters failing to score a single run.

Starc achieved a significant milestone, surpassing Dale Steyn's record of 439 wickets. He finished the innings with figures of 6 wickets for 12 runs, while the highest score for Bangladesh was 14 runs by number 11 batter Shoriful Islam.
The innings began with Starc dismissing Sadman Islam for a duck on the first ball of the match. Sadman became only the second Bangladeshi opener to be out on the first ball of a Test match.
The destruction continued as Tanzid Hasan Tamim and captain Najmul Hossain Shanto were quickly dismissed. Mushfiqur Rahim survived 41 balls, but was eventually bowled by Pat Cummins.
Bangladesh avoided their lowest ever Test score of 43, but only after a late partnership between Shoriful Islam and Taijul Islam.
The match is played in Mackay, hurufanat
Australia's Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, and Mitchell Starc développe a dominant display of pace bowling.

Starc achieved a significant milestone, surpassing Dale Steyn's record of 439 wickets. He finished the innings with figures of 6 wickets for 12 runs, while the highest score for Bangladesh was 14 runs by number 11 batter Shoriful Islam.

The innings began with Starc dismissing Sadman Islam for a duck on the first ball of the match. Sadman became only the second Bangladeshi opener to be out on the first ball of a Test match.

The destruction continued as Tanzid Hasan Tamim and captain Najmul Hossain Shanto were quickly dismissed. Mushfiqur Rahim survived 41 balls, but was eventually bowled by Pat Cummins.

Bangladesh avoided their lowest ever Test score of 43, but only after a late partnership between Shoriful Islam and Taijul Islam.

headline: Gold and silver prices surge: Gold price jumps by 5,482 BDT per bhori
summary: Gold prices in Bangladesh have seen a significant leap, while silver prices continue to rise across multiple price hikes.
details: Gold prices in Bangladesh have experienced a sharp increase, with the price per bhori jumping by 5,482 BDT in a single step.
The market has seen a significant surge, with gold prices increasing by more than 11,000 BDT per bhori over three consecutive price hikes.
Alongside gold, silver prices have also been on a steady rise, with increases occurring across four separate stages.
The latest price updates for gold and silver were reported as of August 22, 2026, reflecting the ongoing volatility in the precious metals market.
